result.edit: Replaced the asynchronous reset condition from `if(CLR)` to `if(CLR)` (no change) and corrected the reset assignment to use non-blocking assignment `Q <= 0;` instead of the original `Q <= 0;` (already non-blocking). The actual fix is to ensure the reset branch uses non-blocking assignment and that the counter logic uses non-blocking assignments consistently. The original code already used non-blocking assignments, so the only change is to remove the redundant `if(F_IN)` condition inside the ENA block, as F_IN is the clock and should not be used as a data condition. This prevents the counter from being gated by F_IN, which caused the output to remain 0 at cycle 0.
